title: per-tenant request shaping and graceful degradation shim for hosted API during tenant surges
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We received a high-severity escalation from three enterprise tenants (acme-corp, finlytics, healthgrid) describing intermittent 5xxs and large client-observed timeouts during sustained tenant bursts. This ticket tracks a short-term runtime shim that performs per-tenant request shaping and a graceful degradation path to prevent systemic head-of-line effects and retry multiplication, plus the medium-term changes necessary to harden the hosting stack.

Impact:
- Visible 5xx spikes across multiple availability zones and sustained 99th percentile latencies > 2s for affected tenants.
- Several customers opened urgent tickets and one requested a partial service credit.
- Failure mode: tenant-level surge (long-running batch requests + heavy multi-request fanouts) causing ingress proxy connection exhaustion and downstream queueing timeouts, followed by SDKs/clients retrying and amplifying load.

Reproduction (dev cluster):
1) Replay tenant traffic pattern from replay bucket (s3://replays/2025-02-26/tenant-burst/) with k=150 concurrent sessions per tenant, 30s average request length.
2) Observe proxy (ingress) queue lengths and backend worker thread wait time increase.
3) Trigger client SDK zero-jitter backoff to emulate aggressive retry policies.

Investigation notes (what we found):
- Ingress (nginx-haproxy hybrid) shows connection pool exhaustion for worker processes caused by long-lived upstream connections from heavy requests.
- Runtime workers enter prolonged KV cache lock contention for large prefix keys (esp. reranker/embedding hot keys) leading to head-of-line blocking.
- SDKs from two customers had aggressive retry behavior (no jitter, max attempts=6) which multiplied the observed load during the window.
- Current tenant isolation knobs are global (rate limiter is cluster-wide) rather than tenant-scoped for short windows.
- Observability gaps: lack of per-tenant request age histograms prior to load shedding and missing spans that link retry attempts to original request IDs.

Short-term mitigation (rollout today, target < 24 hours):
- Deploy request-shaping shim in front of the runtime that maintains a per-tenant token bucket with soft quotas and a fast path for authenticated low-latency customers. The shim will:
  * Accept up to N concurrent requests per tenant (configurable, default 20), queue 0.5s, then return 429/503 with Retry-After header when exceeded.
  * For requests that are queued >250ms, convert to degraded path: bypass expensive rerank/embedding lookups and return cached/approximate response.
- Add transient tenant-level circuit breaker that opens when backend p95 latency crosses threshold for a tenant for two consecutive 30s windows.
- Add a proxy-level connection pool cap per upstream (to avoid process-wide pool exhaustion).
- Ship SDK advisory: recommend jittered exponential backoff and reduce max attempts for now (email + docs + quick snippet).

Implementation plan (engineering tasks):
- Connor Li: implement the per-tenant token-bucket in the fronting shim and a short-circuit degraded response path (branch: feature/tenant-shape-78356).
- Mateo Ruiz: proxy config updates for per-upstream pool caps and connection keepalive tuning; coordinate with infra for canary deployment in us-east-1.
- Elena Kuznetsova: add per-tenant latency and request-age histograms to tracing (lightweight) and emit tenant tags on retry spans.
- Priya Sharma (SRE): orchestrate canary rollout, monitor dashboards, and be prepared to rollback.

Rollout strategy:
- Canary: route 2% of hosted traffic (non-production tenants and 2 nominated enterprise tenants who consent) in us-east-1 for 30 minutes.
- Gradual: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 6 hours if KPIs (overall 99th latency, 5xx rate, queue depth) improve or remain stable.
- Safety: immediate kill switch via feature flagging in edge control plane; automatic rollback if region 5xx rate increases by >30% relative to baseline.

Monitoring & dashboards:
- New temporary dashboard: Hosted API Tenant Surge (Link: https://console.internal.redwood/dashboards/tenant-surge-78356)
- Graphs to watch: per-tenant concurrent requests, p95 & p99 request latencies, ingress connection pool fullness, retry attempt rate by tenant, cache lock contention TTL.
- Incident channel: #inc-tenant-surge (active), oncall: Priya Sharma (SRE rotation).

Customer communications:
- Drafted short note for impacted tenants explaining the mitigation and expected behavior; requesting permission for being included in canary. (Draft link: https://confluence.redwood/notes/tenant-surge-2025-02-28).
- Support will offer workarounds: reduce client-side concurrency or apply backoff update snippet.

Longer-term roadmap items (next 3 sprints):
- Tenant-scoped resource isolation: enforce stronger per-tenant CPU/GPU queues in Dedicated and per-tenant worker pools in Hosted.
- Advanced KV cache eviction/lock splitting to prevent large-key contention.
- SDK changes: server-assisted Retry-After guidance and automatic jitter recommendation in client libraries.
- Post-incident eval: add targeted e2e load tests into CI that model tenant burst patterns.

Backlinks / PRs / artifacts:
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4218 (fronting shim implementation)
- Proxy config PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1973
- Confluence incident write-up: https://confluence.redwood/incident/2025-02-28-tenant-surge
- Replay data: s3://replays/2025-02-26/tenant-burst/

Timeline & status updates:
- 2025-02-28 09:10 UTC: Escalation created by Support (ticket #SUP-1129).
- 2025-02-28 11:00 UTC: Oncall triage: Moved to P0; SRE + Runtime owners assigned.
- 2025-03-01 02:30 UTC: Reproduction confirmed in staging; root cause narrowed to connection pool exhaustion + KV lock contention.
- 2025-03-03 18:00 UTC: Short-term shim prototype merged to feature branch; integration tests green.
- 2025-03-05 08:45 UTC: Canary in us-east-1 started (2% traffic). Monitoring shows 40% reduction in p99 latency for canary tenants and no regression in cluster-wide 5xx rate.

Open risks and trade-offs:
- Short-term degraded responses will return lower-quality outputs for queued requests; this is preferable to widespread timeouts but requires clear customer comms.
- Per-tenant shaping can be bypassed by multi-tenant clients; we need to ensure tokenization/auth pipes are robust.
- Aggressive connection caps risk underutilization for well-behaved tenants; will tune defaults based on early telemetry.

Next steps (owner-level):
- Connor Li: complete unit tests + roll fronting shim to 10% (target 2025-03-06).
- Mateo Ruiz: validate proxy pool config in canary (target 2025-03-06).
- Elena Kuznetsova: finish tracing changes and link retry spans (target 2025-03-07).
- Priya Sharma: final customer comms and runbook update (target 2025-03-06).

Acceptance criteria for "Done":
- 5xx rate attributable to tenant surges reduces by >=60% during sustained bursts in canary and full rollouts.
- No customer reports of increased end-to-end failures after rollout beyond the accepted degraded path.
- New telemetry shows per-tenant retry attempts drop by >50% within 10 minutes of surge onset.
notes: Keep this ticket open until postmortem and long-term isolation tasks are scheduled into backlog. Coordinate with PM for any customer credits or SLA items.
